notes.title: Fixed 'Splatter' Move Bug
notes.content: Fixed bug where 'Splatter' (one of Puggum's Move Tomes) wasn't working correctly.

notes.title: Difficulties Update!
notes.content: [p]Fellow Necromancers,[/p][p] [/p][p]Run difficulties have been implemented! There are now 3 different difficulties:[/p][p] [/p][p][b][u]Chill Difficulty[/u][/b][/p][p] [/p][list][*][p]No Modifiers[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]This is the default Difficulty, and exactly the same as the game has been up till now. If you were already enjoying the game and don't want anything different, choose this.[/p][p] [/p][p][b][u]Standard Difficulty[/u][/b][/p][p] [/p][list][*][p]A Monster with at least 60% HP will be auto-selected each Battle (excluding Boss and Final Battles)[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p][b][u]Extreme Difficulty[/u][/b][/p][p] [/p][list][*][p]A Monster with at least 60% HP will be auto-selected each Battle (excluding Boss and Final Battles)[/p][/*][*][p]0-Cost Moves cannot be duplicated with Duplication Orbs[/p][/*][*][p]Cannot see Enemy tooltips before Battle[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][h3]Philosophy behind the changes:[/h3][p] [/p][p]In an ideal world, we would like players to be switching their teams around more than they do currently. Figuring out the optimal way to play a given configuration is fun, and many Monsters can pair well with a lot of others even if it's not necessarily the absolute 'best' team you could assemble.[/p][p] [/p][p]The Standard Difficulty was one we spent a lot of time playtesting (manually, it wasn't coded) just prior to release, and we almost decided to make that the main mode of the game. At the last moment we decided that removing the ability to always choose your team might negatively impact newer players too much, and so decided against it.[/p][p] [/p][p]Now that we have a small but dedicated player base, we're really excited to see what people think! Even though it may seem frustrating at first, we've found it to be more fun overall when you're really forced to make the most out of any given spot, and there is some really interesting counterplay to it as well (such as letting your weaker Monsters take more Damage intentionally so they cannot be force-chosen, or even killing them off entirely and getting a higher chance of Move Tomes for your preferred Monsters),[/p][p] [/p][p]As always, we welcome your [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1pXXz1pp9QVjT8iF2uK59l1CIbTdN5a1WKk10OLmkD2k/viewform"]feedback![/url][/p][p] [/p][h3]Additional Changes:[/h3][p] [/p][p][u][b]Can no longer exit the run and re-enter to reset Move Tomes (or the Monster chosen for you on higher Difficulties)[/b][/u][/p][p][/p][p]With the introduction of Difficulties, we have decided to remove the ability to 'reset' what Move Tomes you are offered by exiting the run and reloading it. We received feedback from multiple players who wishes this wasn't a possibility, as they felt pressured to take advantage of it. [/p][p][/p][p]Resetting a Battle can still be accomplished using this trick however, including at higher Difficulties (though the Monster auto-chosen for you will not change, you can change who you pair it with). [/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Volcurtle Battle (end of Night 3)[/u][/b][/p][p] [/p][list][*][p]Both Volcurtles have been slightly nerfed - gaining 5 Block on the non-Eruption turn (was 10), dealing 5 Damage (was 10), and gaining 2 Power (was 5). Their HP has also been reduced to 105 (was 120).[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]Most players agree that this Battle can be a run-ender if you're newer to the game, or if you don't have good sources of Block.[/p][p] [/p][p]For now we've decided to make the Battle a little easier, but if this isn't enough we may choose to switch its location to a later night.[/p][p] [/p][p][b][u]Additional Achievements[/u][/b][/p][p][/p][p]3 more Steam Achievements have been added to the game; one for completing a run on each Difficulty. All other Achievements can be completed on any Difficulty, and nothing has been reset.[/p][p][/p][h3]What's Next?[/h3][p] [/p][p]Our next update will include additional Enemies. Ideally we would like every non Boss/Final Battle to have 2 options, and all Boss/Final Battles to have 3 possible options. This will likely come out over the span of 2 updates as we also look to rebalance our existing Enemies (particularly with the new difficulties).[/p][p] [/p][p]We are also moving to fortnightly updates to ensure everything continues to run smoothly and as bug-free as possible. Any reported bugs will of course be fixed ASAP (ideally within 24h!).[/p][p] [/p][p]Happy reanimating![/p][p] [/p][p] [/p][p] [/p]

notes.title: Moving to Fortnightly Updates
notes.content: [p]Fellow Necromancers,[/p][p][/p][p]Unfortunately the 'Additional Difficulties' update won't be out for another week, as we've encountered a couple of issues and want to make sure we get it right before sending it out. [/p][p][/p][p]This has brought to our attention the difficulty of maintaining a weekly-update schedule, and have decided to switch to a fortnightly schedule from now on to ensure we have enough time to do things properly.[/p][p][/p][p]We will of course continue to patch any bugs or issues that we become aware of ASAP (proud to say all fixes have been within 24h of us finding out so far!).[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you for your understanding, and we look forward to getting the Difficulties update out next weekend![/p]

notes.title: Fixed 'Momentum Shift' bug
notes.content: Fixed bug where Momentum Shift would sometimes stop halfway through execution if an Enemy it hit died.

notes.title: Disabling CRT Effects (the static/retro filter effects)
notes.content: [p]Fellow Necromancers,[/p][p][/p][p]Recently we have had some feedback requesting we add settings to disable the CRT effects present in-game (ie the 'Static' and 'Rolling Noise' effects). [/p][p][/p][p]This could already be done by dragging both the 'Static' and 'Rolling Noise' sliders all the way to the left, but now there's also a button to do it in a single click![/p][p][/p][p]Simply open the settings, then click on the 'Graphics' tab and you'll see it :) We hope this helps make the process a little smoother for those who prefer to play without the effects.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Fixed Ghost Stories bug
notes.content:
Ghost Stories was showing an incorrect total when Monster was Dazed.

Enemy Eaglins and Dolphedics would also ignore Taunt in specific circumstances (also fixed).

notes.title: Balance Update, 'Weekends Off' Poll Results, plus Roadmap!
notes.content: [p]Fellow Necromancers,[/p][p] [/p][p]Welcome to the latest balance update! See the end for the results of our recent 'Should Necromancers Get Weekends Off?' poll, and a basic roadmap for the future of NFAW.[/p][p] [/p][h3]General Balance Changes:[/h3][p] [/p][list][*][p]The chances of receiving a Monster with extra Moves in the Night 5 Tombstones has changed (decreased).[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]For reference it is now:[/p][p] [/p][p]25% chance to have 0 extra Moves[/p][p]40% chance to have 1 extra Move[/p][p]25% chance to have 2 extra Moves[/p][p]10% chance to have 3 extra Moves[/p][p] [/p][p]Still a good chance to get a Monster that knows at least 1 extra Move, but we wanted it to feel special when you manage to find a Monster with lots of extras.[/p][p] [/p][list][*][p]500+ Poison and 500+ Bleed Achievement[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]This achievement requires a Monster that's applied 500+ Poison AND Bleed. We've added some extra text to the achievement to make this clearer, as we've had a few comments about it.[/p][p] [/p][p]No single Monster in the game is capable of doing this based on its movepool alone, but it can be done (we promise!).[/p][p] [/p][p]Most of NFAW's achievements are relatively straight-forward to complete once you're familiar with the game, so we wanted one that takes a bit more finesse to complete. We've tested multiple ways to make sure it can be done in 1-2 runs max though, once you figure out how you want to accomplish it (and ideally have an optimal Starter to choose).[/p][p] [/p][p]Generally speaking, it's likely best to leave this achievement until one of your last to complete, as by then you should have a clear choice of which Monster is best to use.[/p][p] [/p][h3]Monster Changes:[/h3][p] [/p][p][b][u]Ausaroo:[/u][/b] [/p][list][*][p]Raw Knuckle now causes an Enemy to lose 8 HP (was 10)[/p][/*][*][p]Encouragement now costs 1 (was 0) and starts at 1 Power (was 2)[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]Despite the recent change to Encouragement, it's still been a little too easy to assemble disgusting builds with Ausaroo. Broken builds are what we want in NFAW, but we want you to have to work for it! Before simply duplicating Encouragement was enough to 'go off', whereas now with it at 1 at least duplicating it will mean taking some time off before you can start one-shotting everything.[/p][p] [/p][p]Raw Knuckle is arguably the best base Offensive Move in the game, so we hope that taking that down a smidge will also help keep Ausaroo in check.[/p][p] [/p][p]We have picked on Ausaroo a fair bit recently, but with it being a starting Monster we feel it's important we get this one right. We want Ausaroo to be a fun first choice before players branch out, rather than feeling like they should use it as their starter every run.[/p][p] [/p][p][b][u]Gargon:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Sage Aggression now deals 9 Damage (was 10)[/p][/*][*][p]Archaic Blessing now gains 9 Block (was 10)[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]Tiny nerf here just to keep things in line after the recent changes to Gargon.[/p][p] [/p][p][b][u]Geckalik:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Measured Force now costs 1 (was 2)[/p][/*][*][p]Coiled Defense now costs 1 (was 2)[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]Players have noted that Geckalik's play pattern of needing to take most (if not all) of every second turn off isn't much fun.[/p][p] [/p][p]We understand that, and our aim with a Monster like this (or Workull, who works similarly) is to have each turn feel like a mini-puzzle where what you do now will impact future turns.[/p][p] [/p][p]When Geckalik's base Moves each cost 2, this just wasn't working out. Hopefully at 1 it's more interesting (and fun!).[/p][p] [/p][p][b][u]Gruthlin:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Inheritance now gains 5 AP (was 6)[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]Another small adjustment where we were a little too ambitious with our original estimates![/p][p] [/p][p][b][u]Hexiboar:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Now starts with '(1) Revival DEF - Only useable after a 'Blind Charge'. Hexiboar restores 6 HP. Forget.'[/p][/*][*][p]Close Your Eyes now costs 1 (was 2)[/p][/*][*][p]Survey the Enemy now reads 'Gain 1 AP for each 'Blind Charge' used this Battle. Forget.'[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]Hexiboar has long been a fan-favourite of players who love to smash face! But we felt it could use a little improvement.[/p][p] [/p][p]Blind Charge is powerful, but takes some time to get going. To help with that, we added Revival to help you restore some HP lost along the way, and reduced the cost of Close Your Eyes to help you set up quicker.[/p][p] [/p][p]Survey the Enemy used to just give Exposed, which felt a little underwhelming on Hexiboar. Exposed is extremely powerful, but feels a little redundant as by the time it's good with Blind Charge, the Move is likely already dealing a ton of damage.[/p][p] [/p][p]We hope that by changing it to an AP gain, it'll be fun to figure out the best time to use it based on what you've paired your Hexiboar with.[/p][p] [/p][p][b][u]Puggum:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Now starts with 50HP (was 40)[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]Puggum has a very unique play pattern in that you want it taking Damage early on in a Night/Battle, and then either healing it just before the end (or keeping it damaged if you have Reconstitute/Splatter).[/p][p] [/p][p]We want Puggum to be something players are really excited to try out, rather than skeptical whether it's worth trying. Some extra HP should help with that![/p][p] [/p][p][b][u]Vastihart:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Thrash now deals 30 Damage (was 25)[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]Similar to Puggum, Vastihart has some cool interactions and play patterns that are unique to it (eg did you know Self-Destruct counts as a negative affliction?).[/p][p] [/p][p]It's a particularly tough one to balance, as it's worth picking early just to mow-down early Battles before shifting to a different team later. We'd love it if it could be more than just an early-game dominator though![/p][p] [/p][p]Vastihart does have an extra base-Move slot available, so if you have any ideas on how to improve it let us know![/p][p] [/p][h3]Watch List:[/h3][p] [/p][p][b][u]Dolphedic:[/u][/b][/p][p] [/p][p]Dolphedic in general has been a little neglected due to Healing being overpowered in the demo, and hasn't really been looked at since.[/p][p] [/p][p]With harder difficulties coming out soon, we expect that Healing will again play a very important role. If that turns out to be false, Dolphedic will get a buff of some sort.[/p][p] [/p][p][b][u]Nosgum:[/u][/b][/p][p] [/p][p]Takes a while to get going and is still rather reliant on what you pair it with to be successful.[/p][p] [/p][p][b][u]Pengilla:[/u][/b][/p][p] [/p][p]While Pengilla's base moveset is very strong, it does feel like it's maybe lacking a little something compared to other Monsters, and can be a little clunky. Training Day is strong in certain situations, but likely worse overall than other cost-reduction methods.[/p][p] [/p][p][b][u]Vastihart:[/u][/b][/p][p] [/p][p]Another Monster that feels like it could use a little boost (beyond what it received today). It's a really cool design that we'd love to see getting a bit more use.[/p][p] [/p][h3]Results of the recent 'Should Necromancers get weekends off?' Poll + Roadmap[/h3][p] [/p][p]Thanks to everyone who took the time to vote in our recent poll! Almost 80% of voters said they'd prefer the main game mode to be 7 Nights, and/or that development time be spent on other things instead.[/p][p] [/p][p]So with that in mind, here is the current roadmap for the future:[/p][p] [/p][list][*][p]Additional difficulties[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]We're aiming to get this out as next week's bigger update. It should provide dedicated players with the most bang-for-buck in terms of extra things to do for now.[/p][p] [/p][list][*][p]Additional enemies[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]We'd love all Battles to have at least 2 options, and the difficult/final Battles to have 3. We'd like to get these out over 2 more weekly updates (after the difficulties).[/p][p] [/p][list][*][p]A draft mode[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]This will take longer, as there are a bunch of different ways it could be implemented. We'd love to get this out around the end of October ideally, with some beta-testing or soft-launches happening a bit earlier if possible.[/p][p] [/p][p]In addition to the above, there are a couple quality-of-life adjustments we'd like to add such as being able to re-arrange your Moves during Battle. We'll do our best to add these when and where we can, plus any balancing and bug fixes.[/p][p] [/p][p]If you have any ideas, please [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform"]let us know![/url][/p]

notes.title: Couple Bug Fixes Before Balance Update Tomorrow!
notes.content: [p]Fellow Necromancers,[/p][p][/p][p]Just a quick update today to fix a couple of bugs! There will be a balance-patch sometime late tomorrow + the results of our recent poll! If you haven't already told us your opinion on whether the main game mode should be 5 nights or 7, please [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSew8WjoBPz9bmN1DVjuqh5SP3MCXldjEtLyRMAyISXciEItRw/viewform"]have your say[/url]![/p][p][/p][h3]Bug Fixes:[/h3][p] [/p][list][*][p]Succumb was counting total Cursed on all Enemies instead of target Enemy.[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Salvation was removing Cursed for Move purposes, but the Cursed was still triggering when the Enemy dealt Damage. Also added a total to show how much AP you'll gain when using it.[/p][/*][*][p]Specific Move Tomes (those that can only be learned by a specific Monster) were acting a little strange, where the same Monster was repeatedly getting Move Tomes rather than it being totally random. The code handling this section has been rewritten and should be working properly now![/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]A massive thank you to Ljtaw for submitting these bugs! Please consider checking out their [url="https://www.youtube.com/@Ljtaw"]YouTube Channel[/url] if you haven't already - they have a couple NFAW vids up, plus some other cool stuff :)[/p][p][/p][p] See you all tomorrow![/p][p] [/p]

notes.title: Small Balance Update!
notes.content: [p]A couple bugs have been fixed in this small balance update, plus the power Animation has been shortened, mainly to make the Crochop Battle less frustrating![/p][h3] [/h3][h3]Specific Monster Changes:[/h3][p] [/p][p][b][u]Bamlin[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Furious Lunge now deals 18 Damage (was 20)[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]Small adjustment as Bamlin now feels very strong after the last balance patch.[/p][p] [/p][p][b][u]Gargon[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Sage Aggression now costs 1 (was 0) and deals 10 Damage (was 8)[/p][/*][*][p]Archaic Blessing now costs 1 (was 0) and gains 10 Block[/p][/*][*][p]Now knows Political Ambition by default (was a Move Tome)[/p][/*][*][p]Has a new Move Tome: "Secret Technique (1) STR: Only useable after another Move. That Move costs 1 less this Battle. Forget."[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]Gargon was both too good when paired with the right Monsters, and too weak when it wasn't.[/p][p] [/p][p]To help with that, we've lowered the ceiling a bit (by making the refresh Moves cost 1 by default), and then raised the floor a bit by giving it a Move that can teach Moves to trigger the refreshes.[/p][p] [/p][p]It'll still go nuts in the right builds, but now you'll have to work for it a bit more. Ideally, this is what we'd like every Monster to be.[/p][p] [/p][p][b][u]Tripleaf[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Blood Spores now costs 1 (was 0), applies 1 Bleed per Dazed (was 2) and has Forget.[/p][/*][*][p]Fever Dream now gains 2 Block per Dazed (was 4)[/p][/*][*][p]Psychic Bloom now deals 2 Damage per Dazed (was 5)[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]Oh boy is Tripleaf good now! The change to Floral Frenzy in the last balance patch has turned it into a real powerhouse.[/p][p] [/p][p]We're okay with how Floral Frenzy plays now. It scales incredibly quickly, but it's a lot of fun to use. Keeping Floral Frenzy the same means adjusting the numbers on Tripleaf's Move Tomes though, so that's what we've decided to do.[/p][p] [/p][h3]What's Next?[/h3][p] [/p][p]While we continue to wait for more [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSew8WjoBPz9bmN1DVjuqh5SP3MCXldjEtLyRMAyISXciEItRw/viewform"]players to weigh in[/url] on whether we should shorten the game to 5 nights (current feedback suggests no!), we will be looking over the remaining Monster pool to see what changes need to be made.[/p][p] [/p][p]To that one person who asked for Hexiboar changes, it is the next one we'll look at! We agree it could use a little something extra.[/p][p] [/p][p]As always, thanks to everyone who continues to provide [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform"]feedback![/url][/p][p] [/p][p]Happy reanimating![/p]

notes.title: Small Bug Fix + Our Philosophy On Saved Games
notes.content:
[p]Fellow Necromancers,[/p][p][/p][p]First off, thank you to BloodWolfBS who mentioned they were having some issues unlocking a particular achievement. Thanks to them, we realised that certain stats were not being saved correctly for achievements. Achievements worked perfectly if you completed the run in a single sitting, but now things like "Win a run without a Monster dying" and "Use at least 7 different team combinations in a single run" are being tracked correctly when you save your game.[/p][p][/p][p]"Use at least 7 different Monster team combinations in a single run." - This is now checked only after winning a Battle, though if a Monster dies it will still count as a unique team.[/p][p][/p][h3]Our Philosophy on Single-Player Saves[/h3][p][/p][p]Recently a player used our [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1pXXz1pp9QVjT8iF2uK59l1CIbTdN5a1WKk10OLmkD2k/"]feedback[/url] form to point out that Battles could be reset by exiting to the menu and going back in, and this 'exploit' could also be used to reset what regular Move Tomes were offered.[/p][p][/p][p]Both of these are intentional. Our philosophy in single-player games is to let the player have as much fun as possible, and give them opportunities to experiment. If you want to try tackling a particular Battle with a certain team, being able to exit out of the Battle if it goes poorly gives you the freedom to do that without wrecking a run. [/p][p][/p][p]This is somewhat common in other roguelikes (such as 'Slay the Spire'). If you prefer to never reset anything and if you die you die, that's great. We play like that sometimes too! And then sometimes we really want to be able to test a weird combo or interaction we haven't tried before.[/p][p][/p][p]We decided to extend this idea to the regular Move Tomes (that only apply to a single Monster) as well. Sometimes you pick a new Monster and REALLY want to get a particularly Move - and if you really, genuinely want it, you can keep exiting and reloading your save until it's offered to you. 

We're open to feedback on this - if enough players feel like they're forced to reroll repeatedly until they get something 'optimal', then we'll remove this feature. But for now, we want Necromancer For A Week to be about assembling cool combos and weird interactions. And we think this helps players do that, while those who prefer to never reroll are totally free to do so.[/p][p][/p][p]If you feel strongly (either way!) about this, let us know below![/p]

notes.title: New Enemy Battles!
notes.content:
[p]More enemy Battles have arrived at the Citadel! Here's what's new:[/p][p] [/p][h3]3 new Battles added![/h3][p] [/p][p]New Enemy teams have been added to the following encounters:[/p][p] [/p][list][*][p]Night 5, Encounter #7 (difficult Battle)[/p][/*][*][p]Night 7, Encounter #1 (difficult Battle)[/p][/*][*][p]Night 7, Encounter #2 (final Battle)[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]Hopefully this adds a little extra variety to your runs! We're trying hard to add new Battles with interesting abilities to give you more things to test your broken builds against.[/p][p] [/p][h3]Infection changed![/h3][p] [/p][list][*][p]Now reads 'Deal 7 Damage to this Monster. Forget. Will deal 3 Damage to this Monster at the end of its turn if unused.'[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]With the game being released, we found that players were too-easily banking multiple Infections. More builds were able to handle this than we expected, and the 8/2 ratio (8 Damage for using, 2 for not) was too generous. Now, instead of being able to hold onto an Infection for 4 turns and breaking even, if you hold one for 3 turns you'll have taken more Damage than you would have by using it immediately.[/p][p] [/p][p]We'll be keeping an eye on this one, as we will be for the new final Battle (and other Battles in general).[/p][p] [/p][h3]Specific Monster Changes:[/h3][p] [/p][p][b][u]Emoil[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Mind Wipe now reads 'Learn a copy of the last Move another Friendly Monster used this turn. That Monster forgets it. Forget.'[/p][/*][/list][p]Essentially the same effect as before, except that now you don't have to use Mind Wipe directly after the previous Move, allowing it to combo better with Opportunistic Swipe.[/p][p] [/p][h3]Special Move Tome Changes:[/h3][p] [/p][list][*][p]Impersonate now reads 'Learn a copy of the last Move used this turn, except the copy has Forget. Forgotten after 3 uses.'[/p][/*][/list][p]Impersonate already copied the last Move used this turn, but didn't mention it in the text box.
[/p][p]It's also one of the more powerful special Move Tomes, so we added the 'Forgotten after 3 uses' bit to tone it down a little. We want these Moves to be fun and powerful, but not run-warping on their own. We were torn between 2 and 3 uses, but settled on 3 to keep the Move as fun as possible.[/p][p] [/p][h3]What's Next?[/h3][p] [/p][p]We're really proud of where the game is at right now, but understand that it could be even better. Balancing and extra enemies will continue to be added, but we want to take a moment to look at the bigger picture.
 [/p][p]Our main point of contention right now appears to be in the average run length. Sometimes you just squeak over the finish line, but more often than not it feels like broken builds are finalised a little earlier than we'd like, making the final few Battles feel like more of a slog than a fun conclusion.
 [/p][p]We initially went with 7 nights because of the name of the game, but then we realised: What if Necromancers didn't work weekends?!
 [/p][p]We could shorten a run to 5 nights (rejigging each map in the process), but we only want to do this if our community agrees it's worthwhile.
 [/p][p][url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSew8WjoBPz9bmN1DVjuqh5SP3MCXldjEtLyRMAyISXciEItRw/viewform"]So have your say.[/url] Should runs be shortened, or should we focus our attention on adding a harder difficulty and a new game mode? Let us know![/p][p] [/p][p]-------[/p][p] [/p][p]As always, thanks to everyone who continues to submit [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform"]feedback[/url] through our form. Even if we don't enact changes, we read every single piece of feedback we receive.[/p][p] [/p][p]Happy reanimating![/p][p] [/p]

notes.title: Small Balance Update before extra Enemies tomorrow!
notes.content: [p]Additional player feedback has come in - and we've adapted to it as promised! Here's what's new:[/p][p][/p][h3]Bug Fixes:[/h3][list][*][p]Fixed bug where an enemy Mawclaw dying to 'Cursed' could freeze the Battle.[/p][/*][/list][p]Massive thank you to the player who used our [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform"]feedback form[/url] to submit this bug![/p][p][/p][h3]Balance Changes:[/h3][p][/p][list][*][p]Impervious now reads 'Reduces ANY unblocked Damage or HP loss from Moves to 1'.[/p][/*][/list][p]We received feedback from multiple players that being able to use HP-loss Moves to defeat enemies with Impervious felt a little too-easy.[/p][p]This change still keeps Poison & Bleed as ways to get through Impervious, and introduces Cursed as an additional way. Any enemy with Impervious also has some Immunity (which prevents negative afflictions), so we feel that using these alternate methods still requires some effort (whereas HP-loss Moves felt cheesy).[/p][p][/p][list][*][p]The Tombstones at the start of Night 5 can now contain Monsters that already know additional Moves [/p][/*][/list][p]Multiple players have told us that the biggest issue with the game currently is the reliance on having a strong set of 2 Monsters, and then only deviating from those when necessary (such as against Poison or Bleed enemies). We agree, and are currently brainstorming additional ways to force you to change up your team more often (in a fun way).[/p][p]This is our first step towards that. The start of night 5 has extra Tombstones in case the player is running low on Monsters or is looking for something specific (some Monsters are definitely designed to pair better with others).[/p][p]Getting a fresh Monster so late into the run does mean it's typically underpowered compared to your other options, so we're hoping that by adding the chance for each tombstone to have a Monster that already knows some of its Move Tomes (can be 0, 1, 2 or 3 extra!) will make it a more exciting encounter. [/p][p]This is an area we're actively looking on, and really appreciate your ideas if you have them![/p][p][/p][h3]Specific Monster Changes:[/h3][p][/p][p][b]Ausaroo[/b][/p][list][*][p]Dedication now reads "Refresh one of your Monster's Moves at random. Cannot refresh another 'Dedication'."[/p][/*][/list][p]A savvy player pointed out that Dedication could be duplicated, then using one to refresh the other constantly provided an easy infinite for things that care about the number of Moves used. This change will take care of that issue. [/p][p]We also added a 'safety' to the Move, so now it can't be used unless there is a Move available to refresh. [/p][p] [/p][p][b]Nosgum[/b][/p][list][*][p]Absorbent Barrier now costs 1 and gains 7 Block (was 2 and 12 respectively)[/p][/*][/list][p]We've heard feedback that some Monsters are still a little bit clunky compared to others. This change weakens Nosgum a little, but allows you to at least use both of its base-Moves in the same turn rather than needing to alternate.[/p][p]It'll still benefit a lot from a good teammate (and getting Move Tomes), but at least now you're not locked in to only choosing one Move per turn early on in a run.[/p][p][/p][h3]Special Move Tomes Changes:[/h3][p][/p][list][*][p]Death Beam now deals 50 Damage (was 40)[/p][/*][/list][p]As massive fans of the original Pokemon games, we couldn't not pay homage to it with our own version of Hyper Beam. We haven't heard of anyone using it yet and have watched some videos where people weren't excited by it, so we've increased the Damage output to 50 to hopefully make it a little more enticing.[/p][p]It has its own cool animation too![/p][p][/p][p][b]Mutual Reckoning added![/b][/p][list][*][p]2 OFF - 'All Monsters (Friendly and Enemies) lose half their remaining HP.'[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]A player submitted this design, and we love it![/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]Thanks as always to everyone who has taken the time to provide [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform"]feedback![/url][/p][p][/p][p]We'll be back tomorrow with the additional Enemies update.  EDIT: Additional enemies for the difficult encounters will be out tomorrow (21st August) - still hunting down some bugs![/p]

notes.title: First Big Balance Patch!
notes.content:
[p]Fellow Necromancers,

It's been a good weekend so far! Thank you to everyone who has supported the release and supplied [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform"]feedback[/url].[/p][p]
At it's heart, Necromancer For A Week is meant to be about finding synergies and exploited broken builds. However, sometimes Monsters are simply stronger than others, or infinite combos exist that are far too easy to pull off (or simply require too much clicking/spamming).[/p][p]
Our first round of balance changes has brought nerfs to a couple of the biggest offenders, while also giving small buffs to under-utilized Monsters.[/p][p]
Here's the full list of changes:[/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Ausaroo:[/b][/u] [/p][list][*][p]Encouragement now reads 'Target Friendly Monster gains 2 Power, plus 1 for each 'Encouragement' used this Battle.'  [/p][/*][/list][p]We've had multiple players state that while the old version of Encouragement was fun to use, it was simply too many clicks.   We want combos and broken builds to be possible in the game, but we don't want you to have to click 7 million times to execute them. This change is a step in that direction, and one we will be keeping a close eye on.  [/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Aviken:[/b][/u] [/p][list][*][p]Pecking Order now has 'forgotten after use'.  [/p][/*][/list][p]Aviken is already one of the most abusive Monsters in the game, and is almost-always worth reanimating. This should take it down just a smidge.  [/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Bamlin:[/b][/u] [/p][list][*][p]Furious Lunge now deals 20 Damage (was 15)[/p][/*][*][p]One Two Punch now deals 7 Damage (was 6)[/p][/*][/list][p]There was a small period of time in the demo where Bamlin had much higher numbers and was FAR too powerful as a result. We now think we may have over-nerfed Bamlin a little, so have given it a small buff to help it be a better choice through the late game.  [/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Crochop:[/b][/u] [/p][list][*][p]Now knows Endurance (1 DEF - 'Target Friendly Monster gains 10 Block, minus 2 for each previous turn this Battle'). [/p][/*][*][p]Crochop is now a starter (replacing Hexiboar)[/p][/*][/list][p]Crochop has been a fan favorite, but without a way to gain Block it's a little unreliable. Endurance should give it enough of a boost to help you survive long enough to utilise it properly, without totally relying on what you pair it with. [/p][p]This addition also makes Crochop an ideal starter for newer players, so we're making the switch with Hexiboar (who currently lacks a way to gain Block).[/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Emoil:[/b][/u] [/p][list][*][p]Opportunistic Swipe now deals 7 Damage (was 5) [/p][/*][*][p]Now knows Optical Illusion (1 DEF - 'Target Friendly Monster gains 8 Block. Forgotten after 3 uses'). [/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Slight upgrade to Opportunistic Swipe helps bring Emoil in line with the power level of the other Monsters, plus a basic Block Move to make it less reliant on what you pair it with.  [/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Gargon:[/b][/u] [/p][list][*][p]Sage Aggression now deals 8 Damage (was 5) [/p][/*][*][p]Archaic Blessing now gains 8 Block (was 5)[/p][/*][/list][p]Increasing the numbers on Gargon's base Moves to bring it more in-line with the overall power level of the current game.  [/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Hipadile:[/b][/u][/p][list][*][p]Now knows Distraught (1 DEF - 'Only useable if you applied Bleed this turn. Target Friendly Monsters gains 8 Block').  [/p][/*][/list][p]Another Monster we wanted to give a basic gain Block Move to.[/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Ignoptopus:[/b][/u][/p][list][*][p]Now knows Raging Inferno (1 DEF - 'Target Friendly Monster gains 2 Block for each Move Ignoptopus knows')[/p][/*][/list][p]Another basic Block Move, but an incredibly synergistic one that should be fun to use and manage.  [/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Mokkral:[/b][/u][/p][list][*][p]Festering Anger now reads 'Increase Mokkral's Temper by 1, plus 1 for each 'Festering Anger' used this Battle. Forgotten after 3 uses.'[/p][/*][/list][p]We're really happy with this change. It will reduce the number of clicks, while still providing some interesting interactions if you're able to copy the Move.[/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Nellop:[/b][/u][/p][list][*][p]Dizzying Spores now reads 'Apply 2 Dazed to all Enemies. All Friendly Monsters gain 4 Block.'[/p][/*][/list][p]Small addition of some Block to bring Nellop in line with other Monsters.[/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Pengilla:[/b][/u][/p][list][*][p]Recognition now costs 1 (was 2)[/p][/*][/list][p]Recognition is one of the best Defensive Moves in the game, but it's difficult to set up, especially if you need it multiple turns in a row (which some later fights almost require). For now, we're going to test reducing this to 1, but may look at other ways to rejig Pengilla in the future if Recognition proves to be too strong at 1.[/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Puggum:[/b][/u][/p][list][*][p]Now starts with 40HP (was 30)[/p][/*][/list][p]We really like how uniquely Puggum plays, but still wanted to try and bring its power level up a bit. An additional 33% HP should do it![/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Quadipede:[/b][/u][/p][list][*][p]Now starts with 35HP (was 30)[/p][/*][/list][p]Another slight HP buff. Quadipede already has a strong Defensive Move and some cool build possibilities, but it can be a little clunky. Hopefully a smidge more HP will help you set up when you need to.[/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Tripleaf:[/b][/u][/p][list][*][p]Floral Frenzy now reads 'Apply 1 Dazed to all Enemies, plus 1 for each 'Floral Frenzy' used this Battle.'[/p][/*][/list][p]The old version (which refreshed whenever you used another Move), was too easy to go infinite with. This new version should help you build Dazed over time while being less spammy.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you again to everyone who has played & supported NFAW. We will continue to respond to [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform"]feedback[/url] and make changes in a timely fashion.  Please keep an eye out for the next update in a day or two, which will be adding additional Enemies! [/p][p][/p][p][i][b]Please note: Making a large number of changes to Moves like this can cause issues to saved runs for Players. If this is you, we apologize.[/b][/i]            [/p]

notes.title: Game Launch + Roadmap for the future!
notes.content: [h3][b]Necromancers - release day is finally upon us![/b][/h3][p][/p][p]All 7 nights are now available, as are all 40 monsters as promised. We've worked really hard to ensure that every Monster feels unique and has its own playstyle, and we're super excited to see what broken synergies you all find! [/p][p]Player feedback has been instrumental in getting NFAW to where it is today, so please [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform"]keep it coming[/url].  [/p][p]Here's a basic roadmap of what the future looks like from here:[/p][list][*][p]We plan to release a small update with some additional enemies over the next 3-4 days. We were hoping to release with more, but getting the balance just right takes time, particularly for the boss & final battles where we're trying to make the fights more unique.[/p][/*][*][p]Difficulty levels will come next, with the current state of the game serving as the 'standard' difficulty. Harder difficulty levels at this stage will include having at least 1 Monster selected for you per Battle, to force you to think more about how each Monster synergizes with your others, and whether you should spread out your Move Tomes and buffs more. Other ideas include removing enemy tooltips & preventing 0-cost Moves from being duplicated outside Battle.  If you have other ideas for harder difficulties please let us know![/p][/*][*][p]Then more enemies will be released. 3 sets of enemies for each possible encounter is our aim. Enough to keep it interesting but not so random that you cannot plan ahead once you learn the game.  [/p][/*][*][p]Lastly, a draft game mode will be implemented. This was actually our original vision for the game, but jumping straight into a draft-style game with so many Moves was very overwhelming. We hope that once the game has been out for a month or two and players are more familiar with how everything works, draft will add some additional variety and more crazy combos!  This update won't come for a month or two, as we focus on balancing the main game mode and ensuring we get this mode perfect.  [/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p]Thank you again for all your support! As always, if you have any [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform"]feedback[/url] please let us know![/p]

notes.title: Bug Fixes + Small Tweak to Pawmor's 'Shattering Palm'
notes.content: [p]A particularly crafty Necromancer was able to find some small bugs that occurred when using only a single Monster for as much of the run as possible (by letting 1 Monster die in Battle). Those bugs have been fixed, but the tactics have been left in place. Essentially, since Move Tomes are randomly generated when you get up to them based on the Monsters you have available to you, technically having a smaller roster means better chances at the same Monster getting multiple Tomes. Pretty sneaky stuff!   [/p][p]The full game contains additional reasons to have a wider roster, but since this essentially adds some extra depth to the game we're all for it. Very flavourful to kill off your own Monsters for value!  [/p][p][/p][p]In addition to the bug fixing, we have one balance change:  [/p][p][b][u]Pawmor:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Shattering Palm now has forget.[/p][/*][/list][p]Pawmor is one of the strongest Monsters in the game, capable of almost soloing many Battles on its own. Adding Forget to Shattering Palm means you'll need to be more strategic in deciding when to use it, and will need to rely more on your 2nd Monster to finish the job (or use the Cursed triggers from Blightfall if Enemies are attacking you).[/p][p]This change also makes picking the 'Iron Stomp' Move Tome more valuable, which often felt a little underwhelming compared to Shattering Palm.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you once more to everyone who continues to provide valuable [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform"]feedback[/url]. Please keep it coming in![/p]

notes.title: MAJOR Update! Font & Contrast adjusted, more animations, unlockables & more!
notes.content:
[p]Greetings Necromancers,
[/p][p]Big changes have occurred at the Citadel! Almost every facet of the game has been updated, from the font and contrast to animations to new Monsters being added.  [/p][p]Here is a full list of what's been updated: [/p][list][*][p]Slight changes have been made to the font to make it more readable. [/p][/*][*][p]Contrast has been increased dramatically, and a 'brightness' filter has also been added to the Settings. [/p][/*][*][p]Some CRT-like effects have been added to maintain the 'dark', retro feeling of the original colour scheme. Both can be adjusted/switched off in the Settings. [/p][/*][*][p]Keyboard shortcut to cancel a Move mid-target has been added. [/p][/*][*][p]You can now see a Monster's 'Move Tomes' on the 'Monsters' page (assuming you've already picked that Monster or it's available as a Starter). [/p][/*][*][p]Many Monsters have had their Moves changed. [/p][/*][*][p]More Battle animations have been added in an effort to better communicate what's happening in-Battle. Every action should now have its own animation. [/p][/*][*][p]5 new unlockable Monsters have been added. You can view how to unlock them from the 'Monsters' page on the Main Menu. [/p][/*][*][p]Starting Monsters have been changed to 'Ausaroo' and 'Irolo' - two Monsters that tend to play a little more differently from turn-to-turn compared to 'Hexiboar' and 'Mawclaw'. [/p][/*][*][p]Players will now be asked if they'd like to complete the tutorial before clicking Play (assuming they haven't yet completed it, and have not progressed passed the first night of gameplay).[/p][/*][/list][p]Finally, we've decided to shift the release date for NFAW to 15th August (PDT) to ensure the game launches in the best possible state. All of your feedback has led to a more fun and better balanced game so far, and we want to continue that through to release.  A massive thank you to everyone who has provided [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform"]feedback[/url] so far. Please keep it coming in![/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Dazed now more noticeable!
notes.content: [p]Fellow Necromancers,[/p][p][/p][p]Another quick update today! Now if your Monster is Dazed, any affected Move will have its Damage number highlighted in blue in the description text during Battle, and be surrounded by *s as well (eg Deal ]*2* Damage).[/p][p]A couple small balance changes as well:[/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Eyetric:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Combo Barrage is now affected by Power after Damage is calculated, rather than Power being added for each Move used.[/p][/*][/list][p]To remain consistent with how other Moves work, this has been changed back to it's original design. We will continue to monitor Eyetric and see if Combo Barrage is fine as-is, or needs reworking to better align with Power.[/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Irolo:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Brainstorm now costs 2 (was 3) and no longer has Forget[/p][/*][/list][p]Brainstorm felt quite underwhelming as a reward Move, so we're giving it a substantial buff.[/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Mawclaw:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Entrenched now only requires Mawclaw to have Block (was 20 Block)[/p][/*][/list][p]Mawclaw is very powerful, but needs a lot of help to really shine. We're hoping that buffing Entrenched makes Mawclaw a little better to use while you're putting your build together, rather than keeping it on your bench until everything has aligned.[/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Nellop:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Toxic Cut now has Target Enemy lose HP equal to its Poison (was dealing Damage)[/p][/*][/list][p]Slight change in how Toxic Cut works, so it is no longer affected by Dazed, Exposed or Power.[/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Veesting:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Tri-Sting now deals 2 Damage 3 times (was 1 Damage)[/p][/*][/list][p]If your Veesting was Dazed, Tri-Sting would do nothing (1 Damage gets rounded down to 0 under Dazed), meaning in certain fights Veesting could never connect as the Enemies either always had Block, or it was Dazed.[/p][p][/p][p]Will be all quiet at the Citadel over the next 3-4 days as we look into changing the contrast and an additional font for those who find the current one difficult to read. [/p][p]Happy reanimating![/p]

notes.title: Keyboard Shortcuts have Arrived!
notes.content: [p]Just a quick update today to add keyboard shortcuts! You can now set a shortcut for:[/p][p][/p][list][*][p]Selecting the Monster on the left as a Target (after clicking on a Move)[/p][/*][*][p]Selecting the Monster on the right as a Target (after clicking on a Move)[/p][/*][*][p]the End Turn button[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Any other shortcuts you'd really like implemented? [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform"]Let us know![/url][/p][p][/p][p]We also accidentally gave Mokkral 'Festering Anger' as a starting Move in the last update, so we have taken it away again (back to its usual levels of Anger!).[/p]

notes.title: Quality Of Life Update + Balance Changes
notes.content:
[h3]Greetings Necromancers,
[/h3][p]A few balance tweaks and a quick quality of life update this time! 
[/p][p]Targeting now no longer requires you to click a Monster unless there's more than one option. So if there's only one Enemy, your Offensive Move will be used as soon as you click it! It also works for Ally stuff - if it targets another Ally or you only have 1 Monster it'll happen as soon as you click the Move during Battle.
[/p][p]We thought about having it automatically if an Enemy has Taunt, but ultimately decided against it (just in case you've forgotten about Taunt!).
[/p][h3]Balance changes:
[/h3][p][b][u]Eyetric:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Combo Barrage Damage per Move used is now affected by power, instead of the total[/p][/*][/list][p]With the recent nerf to Combo Barrage, we figured it could use a little boost. It's now very powerful with Moves that give Power, but still requires multiple Moves to really go off.
[/p][p][b][u]Hexiboar:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Traumatize now gives a random Enemy 2 Bleed (was target Enemy)[/p][/*][/list][p]We're really trying to make the game less click-intensive wherever we can, especially on these Moves that can be used multiple times in a turn. We think it still works from a flavour standpoint - seeing your Ally get Blind Charge'd would be pretty Traumatizing!
[/p][p][b][u]Irolo:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Cultivate Focus now costs 1 (was 2), but teaches Patience to a random Monster that doesn't already know it.[/p][/*][/list][p]Irolo was pretty clunky to play, so we made this change to help with that. Having a huge list of Moves is now much harder, but it's less finicky to use.
[/p][p][b][u]Mokkral:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Escalating Fury now works correctly with Dazed.[/p][/*][*][p]Festering Anger now forgotten after 10 uses [/p][/*][/list][p]Escalating Fury was bugged with Dazed (Dazed was essentially having no effect).[/p][p]Festering Anger was nerfed because it was our first infinite! Turns out if you used Aviken's 'Strategic Inquiry' to copy Festering Anger, they would trigger off each other and you could get your Temper as high as you liked. 10 uses should still let you get plenty of Temper quickly![/p][p]We're not against infinites in theory, but one this simple to achieve seems a little too good.
[/p][p][b][u]Nellop:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Dizzying Spores now adds 2 Dazed to each Enemy (was 1)[/p][/*][/list][p]We talked about potentially changing this Move last update, and decided to give it a shot. Dazed is now worse with the longer nights and no healing after each Battle, so we figure getting an extra dose of it will help.
[/p][p][b][u]Pawmor:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Do As You Did now costs 1 (was 0)[/p][/*][/list][p]Pawmor is really strong in this current iteration of the game, so we're taking it down a notch.
[/p][p][b][u]Boss Changes:[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Double Veesting[/p][/*][/list][p]We fixed a bug which was softlocking the game if a Monster died to a multi-attack at the wrong time, and buffed the fight. We had multiple people say that this fight was much easier than facing the Volcurtles, so hopefully they're a little closer in power level now.
[/p][h2]What's Next?[/h2][p]We're still taking a look at the colour contrast and the font, plus:[/p][list][*][p]Keyboard Shortcuts (for 'End Turn', and possibly selecting left/right targets)[/p][/*][*][p]Adding 5 additional Monsters to unlock
[/p][/*][/list][p]Thank you for all your [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform"]feedback[/url]! Please keep it coming![/p]

notes.title: Tutorial Fixed!

Turns out the Boss Update yesterday broke the Tutorial for ALL players.[/p][p][/p][p]If you tried the game yesterday and this bug affected you, we sincerely apologise. We have now fixed the issue and everything is good to go.[/p][p][/p][p]The Necromancer council will have my head for this, so if you see my corpse out on the grounds please do not reanimate it. notes.title: Boss Battles Are Here!
notes.content: [p]Greetings Necromancers,  [/p][p][/p][p]Boss Battles have arrived at the Citadel! This latest update has a slew of changes:  [/p][list][*][p]Night 2 and Night 3 have new maps, with additional fights.[/p][/*][*][p]HP totals have been reduced across the board for reanimated Monsters. This combined with the new night maps should have the difficulty right where we want it, and you'll need to select your team for each Battle very carefully to conserve HP. Please let us know your thoughts![/p][/*][*][p]A Boss Battle has been added to the end of Night 3. This fight is quite difficult, so try and save your best team for it if you can![/p][/*][/list][p]The following Monsters have also seen Move changes: [/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Aviken[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Offensive Inquiry now costs 1 (down from 2)[/p][/*][*][p]Defensive Inquiry now costs 1 (down from 2)[/p][/*][*][p]Strategic Inquiry now costs 1 (down from 2)[/p][/*][/list][p]The longer nights make taking Damage early more dangerous, and gives you less time to set up. As such, we decided to make the Inquiry Moves cost a little less so you can set up with Aviken repeatedly without it dying.[/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Crochop[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Hopscotch bug fixed[/p][/*][*][p]Intense Glare now costs 1 (down from 2), and is now Defensive (was Strategic)[/p][/*][/list][p]Hopscotch was considered to have been played on the new turn you take, instead of the previous turn when you actually used it. This bug has been fixed.  Dazed has also become worse now that Damage matters more, so Intense Glare received a buff. We will be monitoring other Dazed Moves closely and making additional changes if necessary.  [/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Dolphedic[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Healing Touch now restores 12 HP (was 15)[/p][/*][/list][p]Conversely, restoring HP has gotten much better. Both Dolphedic and Pengilla also suffer from poor play patterns, so there's a good chance both will be reworked in the near future. [/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Eaglin[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Precision Strike now deals 10 Damage (was 15)[/p][/*][*][p]Iron Resolve now gives 10 Block (was 15)[/p][/*][/list][p]Eaglin was proving to be too strong in our testing, providing not only free sources of Damage and Block but multiple Moves in a turn + learning synergies. Both of the Moves it teaches have been nerfed as a result.[/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Eyetric[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Combo Barrage now deals 3 Damage for each other Move used this turn (was 4)[/p][/*][*][p]Shock Exposure now forgotten after 2 uses[/p][/*][/list][p]Eyetric was also very powerful in the right spots. Combo Barrage should be much fairer now, and you'll need to be more strategic with how you use Shock Exposure to give Exposed, rather than just spamming it every turn. [/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Mawclaw[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Stone Relay now costs 0 (was 1)[/p][/*][/list][p]Stone Relay felt like a poor Move Tome and was rarely picked. Hopefully making it free to use makes it more exciting to choose from now on.[/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Mokkral[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Fed Up now requires 10 Temper (was 20)[/p][/*][/list][p]Initially we were concerned Fed Up would be too powerful, but in our testing 20 Temper took far too long to get to unless you had other Moves (mainly 'Festering Anger'), and if you did then you didn't need Fed Up. We're excited to see what builds become possible now![/p][p][/p][p][b][u]Veesting[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p]Take Advantage now refreshes the last Move you used this turn (was random)[/p][/*][/list][p]Veesting is one of our favourite designs, but sequencing with it is quite difficult. Changing the Refresh from random to the last Move used makes it a little easier to plan out your turn.[/p][p][/p][h1]WHAT'S NEXT?[/h1][p]We believe we have the difficulty in a great spot now. We'll still be making balance changes (and looking very carefully at Dolphedic and Pengilla), and we need to add in some more Monsters to unlock in the demo.  [/p][p]We also want to look at some quality of life features, such as:[/p][list][*][p]Improving the font, and possibly adding a setting to change it to a more readable font[/p][/*][*][p]Keyboard shortcuts[/p][/*][*][p]Auto-targeting setting if only 1 target is possible[/p][/*][/list][p]We're also considering changing the contrast of the colours to make things a bit easier on the eyes. We've heard this from a couple of players, but others have had no problem with it. Please [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform"]weigh in![/url][/p][p][/p][p]Thank you to everyone who has been giving us [url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform"]feedback[/url] and helping to make NFAW the best it can be!   [/p]

notes.title: MAJOR Update! New Tutorial Run, ALL Monster movepools changed, ALL NEW Enemies!!
notes.content:
Fellow Necromancers!

The Citadel has been completely reworked after your feedback! Almost every facet of the game has been redone, including:

[list]
[*] A new tutorial run has been added to make the game easier for new players to understand. It only takes approximately 5mins to complete, and walks the player through a simple build to help them understand how to build synergies between their team. [b]This has been enabled for all users by default, but can be skipped by unchecking 'Replay Tutorial Map' in the settings[/b].

[*] Movepools for all Monsters have been reworked! The demo now contains 15 Monsters (the missing 5 will be re-added as unlockables in the next Update) with all-new movesets. We heard your feedback that many Monsters were lacking Defensive options out of the gate, and have made sure that every Monster now has some way of protecting itself, as well as dealing Damage.

[*] Monsters no longer heal after every Battle. Instead, your Monsters will only be healed once you return to the Citadel at the end of a night, and any Monsters that die during Battle will be lost for that run. Now that every Monster has a way of defending itself we wanted to make sure you couldn't simply smash your way through each encounter without consequence.

[*] Move Tomes have been changed. Instead of offering a random Move any Monster could learn, they now randomly pick from a pre-defined set of Moves and can only be taught to a specific Monster. This makes them much more exciting to find, and should help you create much more synergistic builds. This is the change we're most excited about!

[*] Battle Encounters now feature all new Enemies, tailored to that point of the night. No more randomly hitting a super difficult encounter early! This should help the nights have a better difficulty curve as you progress through the run. More variety will be in the full version of the game.

[*] Intents now have tooltips! You can now hover over an intent to see if it's 'Applying Poison' or 'Applying Exposed', etc.

[*] Many keywords and tooltips have been rewritten for better clarity.
[/list]

We hope this helps those of you who found the game a little difficult or daunting to get into, while also providing more interesting decision points with the new Move Tomes for those who were already in and having fun.

A massive thank you to everyone who provided feedback!! Please continue to do so - we love hearing it.

[h1]What's next?[/h1]

Here's what's planned for the next update:

[list]
[*] the 5 Monsters that were taken out of the demo will be re-added as unlockables. We were hoping to get them into this update, but weren't able to get their movepools to a good place in time.

[*] A final boss battle! We've heard feedback that some players would like a final challenge for the demo to really test out their builds. Boss battles were already in the full version, so the encounter will be reworked to fit the demo.

[*] The font will be tweaked slightly to increase readability. 
[/list] 

As always, we welcome your [url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform]feedback[/url]!

Happy reanimating,

 - QuietPenguin

notes.title: Nosgum Gets Revenge!
notes.content:
Greetings fellow Necromancers!

We've had some feedback from players that it's easy to get stuck without a way to win (you really need to make sure you have at least 1 offensive-style Monster on your team, and keep it alive!).

Nosgum has heard this feedback, and it's angry. So angry infact, its learned a new Move:

[i]0 - Revenge (OFFENSIVE)
Deal Damage equal to the amount of HP your monsters have restored this turn.[/i]

Now if you prefer to play stall strategies with Nosgum as your starter, you can still punch hard!

Time for Revenge.

[h2]Other balance changes:[/h2]

[i]- Hold Tight no longer applies Exposed to the user.[/i]

In the demo version of NFAW, Wrap is much less prevalent. As such, there's no need for Hold Tight to have any drawback. If you get this with Geckalik, go nuts (it's a great way to complete the 99 Damage challenge & unlock a new Monster!).

[i]- Planning to Plan now only gives 2 AP, but doesn't disable any Moves.[/i]

We want people to have fun in the demo, and be excited about the Move Tomes they find, so Planning to Plan is losing its drawback, but giving a little less AP (from 3 to 2). 

Let's see what you can do with it! There's a particular unlockable Monster (that requires you to deal 99 Damage with a single hit), that could be broken with this version of Planning to Plan, but let's see what happens!

[h1]What's next?[/h1]

Over the next week we're planning to add some more enemies to the demo version, and rejig how the enemy encounters work a little. 

At the moment you can encounter any enemy at any time (except the first battle which will always be against a single Monster), so it can be a little punishing for new players if they encounter a tough fight early.

For our more experienced players, the full version will contain harder difficulties so don't worry! We're just trying to get the basics down here so we can have NFAW appeal to as many people as possible.

As always, we welcome your [url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScD7SWO5WZGIGfhMFuRukSnSW6-eB_gxApWhB2Sfko1lgQsNg/viewform]feedback[/url]!

Happy reanimating,

 - QuietPenguin

notes.title: Demo is out now!
notes.content:
[h1]Demo is Out![/h1]

I'm excited to finally get the demo out there and gather some feedback to ensure the game is fun and the balance is on-point.

Features include:

[list]
[*] 20 Monsters total (14 immediately available, 6 to unlock).
[*] 2 Monster options for Starters (finish a run to unlock a random available Monster as a Starter, all 20 monsters can be Starters).
[*] 21 Move Tomes to teach to your Monsters
[*] 6 Different Enemies to face, each with unique patterns to learn and counter
[*] 3 Nights' worth of gameplay in each run (7 in the full version)
[/list]

With the demo out, I'm looking to gather feedback about difficulty (only 1 difficulty in the demo, which will become 'Normal' mode upon release) so I can make sure the base gameplay is right, as well as any general UI issues.

[list]
[*] Is the game too difficult? Too easy?
[*] Is the UI clear?
[*] Was anything confusing? eg did you know that monsters can learn an unlimited number of moves?
[/list]

Small updates to the demo will come over the following days as feedback trickles in, plus a new game mode in time for the Next Fest.

Don't forget to wishlist!
